day.note: Alex's Hawk visit to Drew should appear on my Owl list, and it doesn't, so Alex's claim is false. I'll throw one low card at Alex and say why.
The case against Alex is already on the table. I'll stay quiet and vote in eggsecution.

day.text: Alex, a Hawk visit to Drew would have appeared on Blair's Owl list, and it didn't. Your claim doesn't fit. I'm throwing at Alex.
day.note: Alex's Hawk visit to Drew should show on Blair's Owl list, and it doesn't. That conflict points at Alex, so I'm voting Alex with low cards.

day.text: Alex, your Hawk claim doesn't match Blair's Owl list or my Eagle report. Blair's list names the Mouser, and you're the only one who can be it. I'm throwing at Alex.
day.note: I'm Farm this round. Blair's Owl list fits my Eagle report with Alex as the Mouser, and Alex's Hawk claim doesn't appear on that list, so I'll throw at Alex.

day.text: Blair, your Owl list is the only thing anyone is using to hang me, and it can't show my visit to Drew either way. I'm throwing at you.
day.note: Everyone is throwing at me, so I'm likely eggsecuted. A tie or Blair on top would still favour Meowfia, so I'll put five cards on Blair and keep my King.

Alex.note: I'm Meowfia, the Mouser, with a Wink. Drew leads the scoreboard by a lot, so I'll visit Drew to learn their role and decide whether to Wink them.

Blair.note: I'm the Owl. Drew leads the scores, so I'll visit Drew to learn which animals visit them.

Casey.note: Tit visit again. Pigeon can be held by several players, so it's the best single-role guess. Visiting Ellis as a first target this round.

Drew.note: I'm Farm Kookaburra. Ellis has given conflicting roles, so learning Ellis's true role is the most useful check.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm Falcon again. Drew leads by a lot, so I'll visit Drew to learn who they visited and test their story.

Finley.note: I'm Farm Eagle. Drew leads with 18, so I want information on them. Visiting Drew shows who came to them.

Alex.feeling: Tense: I'm the Mouser with a Wink already spent on Drew, and the table has converged on me, so I'm likely to be eggsecuted.

Blair.feeling: Messy and frustrating: Alex's Hawk claim doesn't fit my Owl list, but I can't prove it, and the vote is close.

Casey.feeling: Round 3 feels messy and contested: Drew's wink, conflicting Owl and Hawk claims, and a split vote make it hard to trust anyone's numbers.

Drew.feeling: Frustrating: I was collapsed and confused, so my information was unreliable, and the table is now split between Alex and Blair over a Mouser claim I can't verify.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and muddled: the Owl list, Alex's Hawk claim and Drew's collapse don't fit cleanly, so I'm not confident in any single read.

Finley.feeling: Tense and muddled: the Mouser/Owl list and Alex's Hawk claim contradict each other, and Drew's collapse makes it hard to tell who is lying.

Alex.note: Same plan: put five cards on Blair, keep my C13. A tie or Blair on top favours Meowfia.

Blair.note: Alex's claim still conflicts with my Owl list, so Alex stays my target. I'll throw another low card.

Casey.note: Alex's Hawk claim conflicts with Blair's Owl list, and Alex's accusation is weak. Throwing the same low cards at Alex again.

Drew.note: I'm dead, so my cards don't vote but still score. Alex is the only unclaimed visitor to me and the Owl list, and Alex's Hawk claim doesn't fit it. I'll throw my highest card at Alex.

Ellis.note: The table has converged on Alex, and Alex's Hawk claim fails Blair's Owl list. I'm Farm, so I'll throw at Alex with an 8 that banks if Farm wins.

Finley.note: Several players are throwing at Alex, so I'll add votes with my two Wilds, which cost nothing if they bank.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle and Owl visit-count rules were hard to pin down: it wasn't clear whether a visitor to a player counted when that player was the one making the claim, which caused a long argument about Blair's +1 in round 1.
Alex.fun: Round 2 was a satisfying read: Blair and Drew both claimed Hawk and the table had to work out which claim broke, and Finley's Sphinx claim was hidden in the noise.
Alex.change: Make the dawn report say explicitly who visited whom in a way every role can check, so counts stop being arguable.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I claimed Hawk with a false visit to Drew when I should have stayed quiet or claimed a neutral role, because the Owl list made my claim easy to hang; I'd have kept my cards out of the throw.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle's egg count: I assumed my own visit to Casey didn't count, but the table insisted my visit counted as a visitor, and the dawn report said otherwise. That confusion cost me the round-1 vote.
Blair.fun: Round 3's Owl read on Drew gave a clean visitor list (Eagle, Falcon, Mouser), and the table tracked it into catching Alex as the hidden Mouser.
Blair.change: Make the dawn reports state explicitly whether a player's own visit counts toward the target's visitors, so the egg-count arguments don't waste days.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I should have checked whether my own visit counted before insisting on my account, and I should have stayed quiet about the rule instead of arguing it. In round 2 I wrongly claimed Drew was lying about Hawk; the better play was to keep my throw on Alex's count mismatch.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule was hard to pin down: I initially read "visitors" as including the Eagle's own visit, and that confusion cost us a wrong throw at Blair in round 1. Visitor counting to a target, versus the visitor's own visit, was the sticking point.
Casey.fun: Round 3 was fun: Finley's Eagle report and Blair's Owl list lined up on Drew's visitors, and Alex's Hawk claim fell apart when the Owl list didn't show it. Watching the table test claims against egg counts was satisfying.
Casey.change: I would make the dawn reports name each visitor's role, not just the visitors' names, so claims can be checked more directly. It would reduce the guessing about who visited whom.
Casey.regret: In round 1 and round 2 I joined the group throws at Blair, a Farm player, without enough evidence, and lost those cards. Next time I would hold my cards, or throw at the player whose claim I could verify myself, instead of following the consensus.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle and Owl visitor counts were the most confusing part. It was unclear whether a player's own visit counts toward the target's visitors, and the table argued about it for most of round 1.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: Drew's collapse and the Owl-list accusations turned the whole table on Alex, who was actually Meowfia.
Drew.change: Spell out in the rules whether a player's own visit counts toward a visited player's visitors, and whether Owl lists include the Owl's own visit.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I threw my 13 and 5 at Blair, who was a Farm teammate, on a count argument I hadn't checked. I would have held those high cards and thrown low ones, or checked the visit rule first.

Ellis.confusing: Whether a player's own visit counts as a visitor to the player they visited, since Blair's Eagle count and the Owl list both depended on that. The table spent a whole day arguing it.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when Blair's Owl list showed no Hawk visit to Drew and that exposed Alex's claim. The count-checking made the Meowfia visible.
Ellis.change: State explicitly in the rules whether visits from the reporting player count toward egg totals, so players don't spend days on that question.
Ellis.regret: In Round 2 I threw at Blair, a Farm player, on a Hawk clash I hadn't verified, and lost that round's cards. I should have thrown at Drew, who was Meowfia and whose claims kept failing, and I would have banked the win.

Finley.confusing: Whether a player's own visit counts as a visitor to their target for the Eagle's egg count; the table argued about Blair's +1 for most of round 1. The Owl's "visitors other than yourself" wording also made Blair's list easy to misread.
Finley.fun: Round 2, as the Sphinx, I had to blend in while the table fought over Hawk claims, and Blair ended up eggsecuted by our combined throws. Round 3's Drew collapse after the Mouser list was a tense moment.
Finley.change: Spell out in the rules whether a visit by the Eagle or Owl counts toward the target's visitor total, so the table doesn't spend a day arguing about the arithmetic.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I joined the throw at Blair, who was Farm, after their correction about the Eagle count fit the card text, which cost my side the round. I would have held my cards and questioned Blair's report instead of piling on.

review.title: The Drew Runaway
review.headline: Drew banked a 15-point Meowfia win in round 2 and was never caught.
review.summary: Round 1 was a long argument over how the Eagle counts eggs, and the table eggsecuted Farm Blair. Round 2 repeated this: Blair was killed over a Hawk clash, and Meowfia Drew banked 15 points. In round 3 Alex winked Drew, but Blair's Owl list exposed Alex and Farm won. Drew still won by 13 points.

rounds.recap: Ellis the Floofer hugged Casey and claimed Hawk. The table misread the Eagle's egg rule and decided Blair's +1 should have been +2. Blair was eggsecuted as Farm. Ellis won while throwing only a Wild.

Drew (Floofer) and Finley (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Drew falsely claimed Hawk, which clashed with Blair's real Hawk. The table leaned on Blair because of the round 1 mistake. Both Meowfia threw at Blair and won. Drew banked 15 points.
Alex the Mouser winked leader Drew mid-day. Blair's Owl list named a Mouser. Alex claimed Hawk, which that list did not show. Everyone threw at Alex, who was eggsecuted, so Farm won.

highlights.text: Drew claimed Hawk against the real Hawk, Blair, and steered the table onto Blair.
Alex winked Drew, the score leader, mid-day, and nobody learned who winked.
Blair's Owl list named a Mouser, and Alex's Hawk claim missed that list, so Alex was exposed.
Drew threw two high cards and banked 15 points, which decided the game.

confusions.what: Said the Eagle gains an egg per visitor to Blair, when it counts visitors to the player the Eagle visits.
Counted Blair's own visit as a visitor to Casey, so Drew argued for +2.
Flipped on whether Blair's visit counted as a visitor, and accepted Alex's wrong count.
Called Blair's Eagle count a lie, though a fair misreading of the card made the claim plausible.
Said roles don't change between rounds, then retracted it.
Treated Ellis's and Finley's round 1 and round 2 claims as contradictions, though roles are redealt each round.
Used Blair's round 1 false Eagle claim as proof of lying, though Blair had claimed it truthfully.
Said Drew was the Hawk visitor to Finley, which contradicted Casey's own point that Finley visited Drew.
Argued the Owl list excludes Owl's own visit, which is correct, but missed that Finley's +3 already named Alex as the third visitor.
Said Blair's Owl list was wrong because it left out Blair's own visit, which is how the Owl works.

worked: The Mouser Wink in round 3 made a real moment. Alex killed the leader, and the Owl list then gave Farm a fair deduction.
The Owl's visitor list against the Eagle's +3 egg count gave players a way to check each other's claims.
The one-Hawk rule (each non-buffer animal to at most one player) created a clean contradiction in round 2.
Throw sizes and the best-card-returns consolation gave Alex and Blair a small reason to vote even when losing.
problems: The Eagle card wording is unclear. A whole round was spent on a misreading, and Farm killed their own Eagle. Fix: spell out that it counts visitors to the target and whether the Eagle's own visit counts.
The score swing is too big. Drew banked 15 points in one round as Meowfia and led for the rest of the game. Consider capping how much a single throw can bank, or catching the leader up.
Meowfia don't know each other, and the Floofer and Sphinx in round 2 barely mattered. Hugging a Sphinx did nothing. The cat roles often have no effect.
Players kept treating last round's claims as evidence. Roles are redealt, but the table's reasoning did not reflect that. Say it at the start of each round.
The Hawk claim clash in round 2 had no way to resolve it, so the Farm side voted on a guess. A real Hawk needs a way to prove the role or share the result.
